newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London remained near opening levels in quiet trade ahead of the three-day weekend in London and Hong Kong. Most-active October closed up $0.70 at $352.40 a tonne, while December ended flat at $345.90. The LCE is closed on Monday due to a public holiday and re-opens on Tuesday, August 27.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed barely changed from opening levels as most producer selling and trade buying framed the day's activity. The market was limited on the upside because producers lowered their pricing ideas from recent days, but on the other hand there was no followthrough selling which kept the market limited on the downside, a broker said. Activity was extremely light amid a dearth of fresh news.
The benchmark October contract settled unchanged at 11.85 cents/lb, while March ended 0.01 higher at 11.46. The back months finished flat to 0.06 higher.

AUSTRALIA - Sugar exports in February 1996 fell back to 86,193 tonnes, raw value, against 275,285 tonnes in January and 164,973 tonnes in February 1995. This brought cumulative exports in the first nine months of 1995/96 (June/February) up to 3.81 million tonnes against 3.68 million tonnes in 1994/95. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 4.48 million tonnes against 3.55 million tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of destination in June/February 1995/96 were Japan with 650,890 tonnes raws against 610,684 tonnes, South Korea with 604,589 tonnes compared to 653,387 tonnes and Canada with 539,824 tonnes compared to 520,321 tonnes.

Australia's role as major white sugar supplier continued growing in June/February 1995/96. Total white sugar exports in that period amounted to almost 180,000 tonnes, white value, against 88,000 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Major countries of destination in 1995/96 were Indonesia with 39,568 tonnes compared to nil and Hong Kong with 22,490 tonnes compared to 5,158 tonnes.

GREECE - The latest beet test results of August 11 show that the country will have a far below average crop. Beet weight reached no more than 61.36 tonnes per ha, down from last year's 69.45 tonnes and the average of 68.06 tonnes. Sugar content at 13.41 per cent was rather low compared to 13.48 per cent achieved in 1995 and the average of 13.58 per cent.

This resulted in a theoretical sugar weight per ha of 8.18 tonnes, 12 per cent down on 1995 and also significantly below the average of 9.20 tonnes. Sugar production in 1996/97 can therefore be estimated at around 260,000 tonnes, down from 287,000 tonnes in 1995/96.

BRAZIL - Sugar exports in July 1996 reached 625,800 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 677,100 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first quarter of 1996/97 (May/July) up to 1.23 million tonnes compared to 1.31 million tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 5.92 million tonnes compared to 4.35 million tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of destination in May/July 1996 were Nigeria with 193,922 tonnes whites compared to 86,751 tonnes, the Philippines with 112,772 tonnes against nil and Russia with 90,399 tonnes compared to 199,284 tonnes. The largest outlet for raw sugar in May/July 1996 was the USA with 84,351 tonnes against 14,928 tonnes.

The state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) said it had tendered for 50,000 tonnes of crystal white sugar to be delivered in Karachi by September 30. The tender notice said shipment was required in full shiploads of 12,500 tonnes each. Bids should be submitted by 0600 GMT on August 31 for immediate opening.

TCP officials said the company had an option with an Indian firm to deliver 75,000 tonnes of crystal white sugar in September at $389.00 per tonne, c&f Karachi. The TCP has already booked 225,000 tonnes of sugar for delivery by August 31.

The Egyptian state's Sugar and Integrated Industries Company said it wanted to buy 25,000 tonnes of loose raw sugar or packed white sugar, buyer's option. The deadline for bids is 0700 GMT on September 17. The company did not mention a date for shipment or delivery and company officials were not available.
